evidence: Read longterm-mem/internal/promote/frontmatter.go in the target worktree. patchedFrontmatter is now only setListField(setScalarField(block, statusField, status), relatedField, related), with no identity handling. PatchStatusFields writes only when newBlock != fmBlock and leaves the body byte-identical.

Read propagate.go and propagate_cards.go. patchPage calls PatchStatusFields and updates only FrontmatterHash. eachCardPatchTarget skips a page when patchedFrontmatter(block, status, related) == block, so a legacy page whose status already matches is never visited, written or counted. It also skips a non-retired memory whose page is not retired.

Grepped the promote package for other identity-rewrite paths outside tests (relabel, rewriteKeys, storeAgnostic, migrate*()). None found. The other PatchStatusFields caller, writer.go:419 (supersede), goes through the same identity-free function.

Read cmd/longterm-mem/page_keys_test.go. TestALegacyCardPageWhoseStatusIsPatchedKeepsItsIdentityLines asserts the patched page equals the original with only the status line changed (byte-for-byte), that the sidecar frontmatter hash matches the page, and that a second sync patches nothing. TestALegacyCardPageWhoseStatusAlreadyMatchesIsNotAPatchTarget runs both dry-run and real sync and asserts no patch is reported and the page is unchanged. TestAPageWhoseStatusIsPatchedCarriesOnlyTheStoreAgnosticKeys covers a store-agnostic page. These match S6 (b) and L64.

Only residual: a retired memory whose page status matches but whose related lines differ in format or content is still patched. That is a legitimate related patch, not an identity rewrite, and it is not a defect of this commit.
Not run: no tests were executed, no git diff was available (read-only access to the worktree files), and the base commit was not compared.
